To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the video footage used in the television coverage of the Euro'92 was poor in quality and that this was not a disadvantage, but rather a guarantee of its status as actuality footage.
the semiotics of actuality is a way of presenting the world that is not only different from the semiotics of fiction, but that is in some respects its opposite.

the Swedish tabloids and Swedish television, in their coverage of the 1992 Euro football championships, used actuality video footage of football fan violence in a way that was both consistent with and helped to create the impression that football violence is both widespread and easily contained, and that the best way to enjoy large-scale sports events is to watch them on television.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the semiotics of television coverage of football fan violence during Euro'92 in the Swedish media.
the semiotics of violence in the context of football and the European Football Championship.

the way television presents itself as an ‘unmediated’ or ‘transparent’ window onto actuality, and with the ways in which the semiotics of this actuality are shaped by other, often competing discourses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the actuality footage of the Euro'92 incidents was used to present the violence as something which was happening elsewhere, and to which the spectator could safely remain distanced.

the actuality footage of football fan violence during Euro'92, in combination with its framing in the media, was a significant element in the construction of a new and more complex semiotics of violent football spectatorship.
television is a medium that has been able to create a semiotics of violence that is both spectacular and reassuring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the semiotics of violent reality is a semiotic of the television.
the semiotics of violent reality is a way of presenting the actuality footage in a way that is both entertaining and safe for the viewer.
the semiotics of violent footage is part of a semiotics of actuality, and that this is part of a wider semiotics of television.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the media is not just a reflection of the world, but an important part of the social world itself.
the semiotics of violence on television are inextricably linked to the semiotics of television itself.
television coverage of violent incidents at sporting events can be analysed in terms of how the technical characteristics of video footage is used to construct a semiotics of actuality.
